assessmentPoints: Seed-identities answers in the opening activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the closing activity
successCriteria: The two seed identities, on the unit circle - the legs are cos theta and sin theta with hypotenuse 1, so sin squared plus cos squared equals one and tan is sin over cos.
objectives.text: Use the seed identities sin squared plus cos squared equals one and tan equals sin over cos

assessmentPoints: Compound-angle answers in the second activity
Trap answers in the fourth activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the closing activity
successCriteria: Compound angles: computing sin 75 degrees - split 75 as 45 + 30, expand with sin(A + B), and the four known values give (root 6 + root 2) over 4.
Misconception: cos(A + B) does not split - cos 60 is 0.5 while cos 30 + cos 30 is about 1.73, so the cosine of a sum is never the sum of cosines.
objectives.text: Apply the compound angle formulae to find exact values such as sin 75 degrees

assessmentPoints: R-form answers in the third activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the closing activity
successCriteria: The R-formula: one wobble, not two - 3 cos x + 4 sin x becomes 5 cos(x - 53.1 degrees) from the 3-4-5 triangle, so max is 5 and min is -5.
objectives.text: Rewrite a cos x + b sin x in R-form and read off its maximum, minimum and period
